title: Process Importance, LMKD, and Memory Pressure Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies process importance, lmkd, and memory pressure?
options: Treat process residence as revocable, use pressure callbacks opportunistically, and make durable recovery independent of warning callbacks.
questions.answer: Treat process residence as revocable, use pressure callbacks opportunistically, and make durable recovery independent of warning callbacks.
questions.explanation: The correct response preserves authority, compatibility, exact artifact evidence, adverse-path behavior, and operational ownership.

questions.prompt: Android always invokes onTrimMemory immediately before lmkd terminates an application process.
questions.explanation: Relying on onTrimMemory as a guaranteed warning before termination leaves recovery broken when the process is killed without that callback.

questions.prompt: What should survive a memory-pressure kill?
questions.answer: Durable user intent and recoverable state, while recreatable caches and process objects may be discarded.
questions.explanation: The answer identifies the contract or mechanism that remains valid beyond one implementation demonstration.
